destination.title: Modulus and gravitino cosmology
destination.question: When do modulus or gravitino production, domination and decay permit BBN-compatible histories and acceptable dark-matter abundances?
destination.summary: Connects decay timing, production, annihilation and dilution while preserving stable-gravitino, thermal-WIMP and nonthermal-neutralino alternatives.

systems: Cosmological moduli and other specified heavy scalars
regimes: Stable gravitinos as a separate alternative
assumptions: Dominance, branching fractions and mass ordering are model-specific
conventions: Successful BBN timing does not by itself certify gravitino, LSP or axion safety
includes: G2-MSSM, LVS and effective decay cosmologies
Superheavy dark matter diluted by a lighter modulus
excludes: Treating every modulus as the producer of the surviving dark matter

sources.title: Non-thermal Dark Matter and the Moduli Problem in String Frameworks

evidence.text: Can moduli stabilization and decay in the G2-MSSM avoid cosmological moduli and gravitino problems while producing an acceptable nonthermal Wino dark-matter abundance, despite a deficient thermal abundance and potentially excessive decay production?

sources.title: Mirage in the Sky: Non-thermal Dark Matter, Gravitino Problem, and Cosmic Ray Anomalies

evidence.text: Can late modulus or gravitino decay produce the correct abundance of TeV-scale, strongly annihilating dark matter, address cosmological moduli/gravitino problems, and explain the cosmic-ray anomalies discussed in 2009?

sources.title: A Non-thermal WIMP Miracle

evidence.text: Can the simple solution of making gravitationally coupled moduli heavy enough to decay before BBN also produce the observed dark-matter abundance through nonthermal WIMPs, and what supersymmetric spectrum does that suggest?

sources.title: Confronting the moduli-induced lightest-superpartner problem

evidence.text: Can hidden-sector extensions of the MSSM avoid excessive LSP production or annihilation signals following reheating by string-motivated, Planck-coupled moduli?

sources.title: Moduli mediation without moduli-induced gravitino problem

evidence.text: Can an additional light modulus dilute gravitinos and nonthermal LSPs produced by heavier-modulus decay, preserving modulus or mirage mediation in both low- and high-scale SUSY-breaking scenarios?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Remnants from the String Landscape

evidence.text: Does a populated modulus decay early enough to restore radiation before nucleosynthesis, and what follows if its mass tracks the gravitino?

sources.title: The cosmological moduli problem and naturalness

evidence.text: Can late-decaying cosmological moduli satisfy BBN, gravitino-production and neutralino-abundance constraints while retaining electroweak naturalness? The paper distinguishes the original BBN problem from moduli-induced gravitino and LSP problems.

sources.title: Moduli-induced gravitino problem

evidence.text: Does making a cosmological modulus heavier than approximately 100 TeV solve its cosmological problems, once gravitino production and subsequent BBN and relic-abundance constraints are included?

sources.title: Gravitino production from heavy moduli decay and cosmological moduli problem revived

evidence.text: Does making moduli heavy enough to decay before nucleosynthesis solve their cosmological problem, once modulus decay into longitudinal gravitinos and subsequent stable neutralino production are treated quantitatively?

sources.title: Non-thermal Dark Matter and the Moduli Problem in String Frameworks

evidence.text: Use the stabilized supergravity mass matrix and canonical eigenstates; expand gauge kinetic functions, matter metrics and Higgs bilinears to obtain decay couplings. Include leading RG effects from top Yukawa and strong gauge interactions and compute two-body widths. Standard-model fermion and three-body channels are neglected as comparatively suppressed.

sources.title: Mirage in the Sky: Non-thermal Dark Matter, Gravitino Problem, and Cosmic Ray Anomalies

evidence.text: Specifies GUT-scale mirage-mediated soft terms and anomalous dimensions, then uses RG evolution to illustrate gaugino and scalar spectra and obtain alternative LSP assignments.

sources.title: A Non-thermal WIMP Miracle

evidence.text: Use the supergravity vacuum potential and small vacuum energy to relate m3/2 to F/mp. Generic quadratic Kähler terms supply scalar mass contributions of order m3/2, motivating a relation between modulus masses and the supersymmetry-breaking spectrum.

sources.title: Confronting the moduli-induced lightest-superpartner problem

evidence.text: The asymmetric model uses separate particle/antiparticle equations with production asymmetry κ and transfer reactions. The non-Abelian model tracks separate sector temperatures and estimates Sommerfeld-enhanced annihilation.

sources.title: Moduli mediation without moduli-induced gravitino problem

evidence.text: The authors use V = e^K(K^{I J̄}D_IW D_J̄W̄ − 3|W|²), solve supersymmetric reference extrema, and expand the uplifted potential to obtain shifts, canonical masses and F-terms.

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Remnants from the String Landscape

evidence.text: Solve section-degree constraints without denominator coordinates, extract minimal divisor factors, and identify the candidate fiber. Check monodromy and matter separately before concluding non-Higgsability.

sources.title: SUSY phenomenology of KKLT flux compactifications

evidence.text: Can KKLT-motivated mixed modulus–anomaly mediation with the MSSM on D7 branes yield acceptable electroweak breaking, a viable superpartner spectrum, and neutralino dark matter under the paper's experimental and cosmological constraints?

sources.title: Correlation between Dark Matter and Dark Radiation in String Compactifications

evidence.text: How generic is dark radiation in perturbatively stabilised string compactifications, and what constraints relate dark matter mass and production history to dark radiation when both originate in lightest-modulus decay?

sources.title: A Bottom-up approach to moduli dynamics in heavy gravitino scenario: Superpotential, soft terms and sparticle mass spectrum

evidence.text: Can automatic alignment of modulus- and anomaly-mediated gaugino phases constrain the moduli superpotential, and yield stabilized moduli, viable MSSM soft terms and cosmology with a gravitino of order 10 TeV?

sources.title: SUSY’s Ladder: reframing sequestering at Large Volume

evidence.text: Can sequestering naturally separate weak-scale gauginos from a gravitino heavy enough to decay before WIMP freeze-out, roughly m3/2 ≳ 10^4 TeV, while remaining stable against quantum corrections?

sources.title: Dark Matter density and the Higgs mass in LVS String Phenomenology

evidence.text: Can high-gravitino-mass LVS inoAMSB phenomenology simultaneously accommodate the Higgs mass, thermal neutralino dark matter, flavor constraints and the cosmological modulus problem, and what would its collider implications be?

sources.title: Moduli decays and gravitinos

evidence.text: When are heavy, approximately supersymmetric moduli or inflatons helicity suppressed in decays to gravitino pairs, and what hidden-sector conditions permit viable cosmology?

sources.title: Wino cold dark matter from anomaly mediated SUSY breaking

evidence.text: Can sequestered-sector/anomaly-mediated supersymmetry breaking permit moduli to decay before nucleosynthesis while producing an acceptable nonthermal Wino dark-matter abundance, and what detection signals would follow?

sources.title: The dark universe after reheating in string inflation

evidence.text: How do correlations among inflation, sequestered supersymmetry breaking, modulus reheating, dark radiation and isocurvature constrain dark matter in fibred type-IIB compactifications with the visible sector on D3-branes?

sources.title: Supersymmetry Breaking due to Moduli Stabilization in String Theory

evidence.text: How does strong volume-modulus stabilization change supersymmetry breaking transmitted to visible matter, and can the resulting spectrum accommodate inflation and alleviate cosmological moduli and gravitino problems?

sources.title: LARGE Volume String Compactifications at Finite Temperature

evidence.text: Can LVS moduli thermalise, do thermal corrections generate new minima or decompactification, and what constraints follow for reheating, internal volume and cosmological moduli dilution?

sources.title: Moduli Thermalization and Finite Temperature Effects in 'Big' Divisor Large Volume D3/D7 Swiss-Cheese Compactification

evidence.text: Can divisor-volume moduli thermalize with visible matter, decay before causing a cosmological moduli problem, and leave the zero-temperature metastable de Sitter minimum intact under finite-temperature corrections?

sources.title: Dark matter and dark radiation from the early universe with a modulus coupled to the PQMSSM

evidence.text: How does a single light modulus coupled to the SUSY DFSZ/PQMSSM sector alter mixed axion–higgsino dark matter, relativistic-axion dark radiation, and possible solutions to the cosmological moduli problem?

sources.title: Lectures on Cosmic Inflation and its Potential Stringy Realizations

evidence.text: Could relic defects from an assumed early phase transition disrupt nucleosynthesis or overclose the later universe?

sources.title: String loop origin for dark radiation and superheavy dark matter in type IIB compactifications

evidence.text: How do logarithmic string-loop corrections affect perturbative Kähler-modulus stabilization, canonical mixing and axionic dark radiation, and can the resulting modulus reheating support nonthermal dark matter and a baryon–dark matter coincidence?

sources.title: Superheavy dark matter from string theory

evidence.text: Can high-scale supersymmetry and late string-modulus domination yield the observed abundance of superheavy neutralino dark matter, despite its overproduction in a standard thermal history, while remaining compatible with inflationary and dark-radiation constraints?

sources.title: Susy at the FPF

evidence.text: Which SUSY-breaking mechanisms can produce a light modulino with active-neutrino mixing accessible through neutrino disappearance at proposed Forward Physics Facility experiments, despite a much heavier gravitino?

sources.title: Dark Radiation and Dark Matter in Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: Can overall-volume modulus decay in sequestered and non-sequestered LARGE volume compactifications generate appreciable axionic dark radiation together with viable dark matter?

sources.title: Moduli induced cogenesis of baryon asymmetry and dark matter

evidence.text: Can late modulus decay generate both visible baryon asymmetry and asymmetric dark matter at GeV-scale reheating, while conserving baryon number at the fundamental vertices and explaining ΩDM/ΩB ≈ 5?

sources.title: A Note on the moduli-induced gravitino problem

evidence.text: Can rapid nonperturbative transfer of modulus energy into Standard Model bosons, through tachyonic resonance, suppress subsequent direct gravitino production, and what approximate modulus-mass range permits this mechanism?

sources.title: Gravitinos from heavy scalar decay

evidence.text: What cosmological constraints follow when a heavy scalar dominating the universe decays into gravitino pairs, and can stable gravitinos permit viable moduli cosmology or a new warm-dark-matter window?

sources.title: Higgs, Moduli Problem, Baryogenesis and Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: Can Affleck–Dine baryogenesis survive entropy production from light-modulus decay in high-scale supersymmetry, while LARGE volume stabilization avoids gravitino and LSP overproduction? The paper also examines Q-ball formation and enhanced inflaton–AD couplings.

sources.title: Cosmology in the presence of multiple light moduli

evidence.text: Can vacuum-misaligned moduli with comparable masses yield viable dark-radiation and dark-matter abundances, and what mass splittings, branching fractions or annihilation processes are required?

sources.title: Affleck-Dine Baryogenesis in Type IIB String Models

evidence.text: Can Affleck–Dine baryogenesis be embedded in sequestered type IIB models, with an inflationary tachyonic AD mass, positive late-time scalar masses, and sufficient asymmetry after dilution by the lightest modulus?

sources.title: The Baryon-Dark Matter Ratio Via Moduli Decay After Affleck-Dine Baryogenesis

evidence.text: Can late moduli decay simultaneously dilute excessive MSSM Affleck–Dine baryogenesis, produce the nonthermal LSP abundance, and explain the historical abundance ratio Ωdm/ΩB ≈ 5?

sources.title: Axionphilic cosmological moduli

evidence.text: When do Kähler-potential derivative interactions permit modulus decay into stringy axions or Nambu–Goldstone bosons without final-state mass suppression, and what does this imply for reheating, dark radiation and axino dark matter?

sources.title: Moduli-Induced Axion Problem

evidence.text: Can a modulus stabilized by SUSY breaking spoil cosmology through decays into ultralight axions even when its mass is large enough for decay before BBN, and which interactions or geometries suppress this production?

sources.title: Cosmological moduli problem in large volume scenario and thermal inflation

evidence.text: When can single or double thermal inflation dilute the light LVS volume modulus sufficiently despite thermally induced modulus reproduction, and can a concrete model also retain successful baryogenesis and dark matter production?

sources.title: Moduli stabilization to a natural MSSM with gravitino dark matter and inflation

evidence.text: Can gravity mediation yield a stable O(100 GeV) gravitino below TeV-scale superpartners while accommodating moduli stabilization, inflation, dark-matter abundance, and the Higgs mass with limited electroweak tuning?

sources.title: Nonthermal dark matter in string compactifications

evidence.text: Can late modulus decay in sequestered type-IIB LARGE Volume Scenarios produce the observed neutralino abundance for both thermal overproduction and underproduction, while avoiding moduli-induced gravitino and axionic dark-radiation/dark-matter problems?

sources.title: Dark radiation in LARGE volume models

evidence.text: How much dark radiation accompanies reheating by the volume modulus in sequestered LARGE Volume Scenario models, and how does ΔNeff constrain visible couplings and additional light sectors?

sources.title: Moduli-Induced Axion Problem

evidence.text: Can a modulus stabilized by SUSY breaking spoil cosmology through decays into ultralight axions even when its mass is large enough for decay before BBN, and which interactions or geometries suppress this production?

sources.title: Loop corrections to $\Delta N_{eff}$ in large volume models

evidence.text: Can MSSM radiative corrections to the volume-modulus Giudice–Masiero coupling enhance visible reheating enough to make minimal large-volume models compatible with the paper's historical Neff constraints? The stated target is Z(mΦ) ≳ 1.2 starting from Z(Mstring) = 1.

sources.title: Dark Radiation in Anisotropic LARGE Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: How does replacing the light volume modulus of minimal LVS with a lighter transverse bulk modulus change reheating and axionic dark radiation, especially when visible-sector soft masses are sequestered by D3-branes at a singularity?

sources.title: Dark Radiation predictions from general Large Volume Scenarios

evidence.text: Can LVS constructions beyond the sequestered case satisfy dark-radiation bounds with minimal visible matter and natural parameters, especially by enhancing modulus decays into gauge bosons?

sources.title: General Analysis of Dark Radiation in Sequestered String Models

evidence.text: How do the visible-sector matter metric, de Sitter stabilization mechanism and split-SUSY scalar thresholds change axionic dark radiation from the lightest modulus in sequestered LARGE Volume models?

sources.title: The Axiverse induced Dark Radiation Problem

evidence.text: Why does a large string/M-theory axiverse not produce excessive relativistic axions through late modulus decay, and which kinetic, mass-mixing or vacuum structures can suppress that dark radiation?

sources.title: String Theory and the Dark Glueball Problem

evidence.text: When do reheated hidden pure Yang–Mills sectors overproduce glueballs, and can preferential visible-sector reheating or decays into moduli or axions yield an acceptable cosmology?

sources.title: On dark radiation from string moduli decay to ALPs

evidence.text: How strongly does dark radiation from lightest-modulus decay into ALPs constrain modulus masses and couplings when the competing MSSM decay channels are included beyond commonly studied sequestered stabilization models?

sources.title: Dark radiation in LARGE volume models

evidence.text: Convert hidden branching fractions into ΔNeff using comoving visible-sector entropy conservation: ΔNeff=(43/7)[fhidden/(1−fhidden)][g(Tdec)/g(Treheat)]^(1/3). Decoupled hidden radiation and visible radiation evolve differently during visible entropy release.

sources.title: Moduli-Induced Axion Problem

evidence.text: Axionic energy injection is translated into ΔNeff using the axion branching fraction, relativistic degrees of freedom at decay and the visible-sector reheating temperature. Constraints on axion and SM partial widths are then compared with model-specific decay channels.

sources.title: Loop corrections to $\Delta N_{eff}$ in large volume models

evidence.text: Randomly scans m0,m1/2 ∈ [0.1,10] TeV, A0 ∈ [−30,30] TeV, tanβ ∈ [1,60] and both signs of µ. Varies mt = 173.2 ± 5 GeV and αs(mZ) = 0.1184 ± 0.0021; retains Higgs masses in [123,129] GeV and includes reheating uncertainty through 3.12κ ≤ ΔNeff ≤ 3.48κ.

sources.title: Dark Radiation in Anisotropic LARGE Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: Expand K=−ln(T1+T̄1)−2ln(T2+T̄2), canonically normalize the bulk moduli, and rotate to volume and transverse mass eigenstates. Derivative axion couplings then determine the lightest modulus's axionic decay width.

sources.title: Dark Radiation predictions from general Large Volume Scenarios

evidence.text: The authors extract modulus decay widths from the Kähler potential and gauge kinetic functions after canonical normalization and integrating out stabilized directions, then infer dark radiation from the ratio of hidden to visible partial widths.

sources.title: General Analysis of Dark Radiation in Sequestered String Models

evidence.text: Use the N=1 supergravity effective action, inverse-volume moduli stabilization and soft-term formulas to compare scalar masses with the volume-modulus mass separately for each matter-metric and uplift case.

sources.title: Correlation between Dark Matter and Dark Radiation in String Compactifications

evidence.text: How generic is dark radiation in perturbatively stabilised string compactifications, and what constraints relate dark matter mass and production history to dark radiation when both originate in lightest-modulus decay?

sources.title: The dark universe after reheating in string inflation

evidence.text: How do correlations among inflation, sequestered supersymmetry breaking, modulus reheating, dark radiation and isocurvature constrain dark matter in fibred type-IIB compactifications with the visible sector on D3-branes?

sources.title: Dark matter and dark radiation from the early universe with a modulus coupled to the PQMSSM

evidence.text: How does a single light modulus coupled to the SUSY DFSZ/PQMSSM sector alter mixed axion–higgsino dark matter, relativistic-axion dark radiation, and possible solutions to the cosmological moduli problem?

sources.title: String loop origin for dark radiation and superheavy dark matter in type IIB compactifications

evidence.text: How do logarithmic string-loop corrections affect perturbative Kähler-modulus stabilization, canonical mixing and axionic dark radiation, and can the resulting modulus reheating support nonthermal dark matter and a baryon–dark matter coincidence?

sources.title: Superheavy dark matter from string theory

evidence.text: Can high-scale supersymmetry and late string-modulus domination yield the observed abundance of superheavy neutralino dark matter, despite its overproduction in a standard thermal history, while remaining compatible with inflationary and dark-radiation constraints?

sources.title: Dark Radiation and Dark Matter in Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: Can overall-volume modulus decay in sequestered and non-sequestered LARGE volume compactifications generate appreciable axionic dark radiation together with viable dark matter?

sources.title: Cosmology in the presence of multiple light moduli

evidence.text: Can vacuum-misaligned moduli with comparable masses yield viable dark-radiation and dark-matter abundances, and what mass splittings, branching fractions or annihilation processes are required?

sources.title: Axionphilic cosmological moduli

evidence.text: When do Kähler-potential derivative interactions permit modulus decay into stringy axions or Nambu–Goldstone bosons without final-state mass suppression, and what does this imply for reheating, dark radiation and axino dark matter?

sources.title: Nonthermal dark matter in string compactifications

evidence.text: Can late modulus decay in sequestered type-IIB LARGE Volume Scenarios produce the observed neutralino abundance for both thermal overproduction and underproduction, while avoiding moduli-induced gravitino and axionic dark-radiation/dark-matter problems?

destinations.title: How much dark radiation accompanies reheating by the volume modulus in sequestered LARGE Volume Scenario models, and how does ΔNeff constrain visible couplings and additional light sectors?

Can a modulus stabilized by SUSY breaking spoil cosmology through decays into ultralight axions even when its mass is large enough for decay before BBN, and which interactions or geometries suppress this production?

Can MSSM radiative corrections to the volume-modulus Giudice–Masiero coupling enhance visible reheating enough to make minimal large-volume models compatible with the paper's historical Neff constraints? The stated target is Z(mΦ) ≳ 1.2 starting from Z(Mstring) = 1.

How does replacing the light volume modulus of minimal LVS with a lighter transverse bulk modulus change reheating and axionic dark radiation, especially when visible-sector soft masses are sequestered by D3-branes at a singularity?
Can LVS constructions beyond the sequestered case satisfy dark-radiation bounds with minimal visible matter and natural parameters, especially by enhancing modulus decays into gauge bosons?
How do the visible-sector matter metric, de Sitter stabilization mechanism and split-SUSY scalar thresholds change axionic dark radiation from the lightest modulus in sequestered LARGE Volume models?
Why does a large string/M-theory axiverse not produce excessive relativistic axions through late modulus decay, and which kinetic, mass-mixing or vacuum structures can suppress that dark radiation?
When do reheated hidden pure Yang–Mills sectors overproduce glueballs, and can preferential visible-sector reheating or decays into moduli or axions yield an acceptable cosmology?

How strongly does dark radiation from lightest-modulus decay into ALPs constrain modulus masses and couplings when the competing MSSM decay channels are included beyond commonly studied sequestered stabilization models?

destination.title: Baryogenesis in modified cosmic histories
destination.question: How can baryon asymmetry be generated or preserved through the specified reheating, expansion and entropy-production histories?
destination.summary: Includes Affleck–Dine survival, decay-generated asymmetry and asymmetric dark matter, with separate access to relaxion leptogenesis, electroweak expansion and conditional FL applications.

sources.title: Electroweak Baryogenesis and the Expansion Rate of the Universe

evidence.text: How does relaxing radiation domination at the electroweak epoch change baryon-asymmetry preservation and the possibility of baryogenesis at a second-order transition or crossover?

sources.title: Moduli-induced Baryogenesis

evidence.text: Tree–loop interference gives mass-dependent CP decay asymmetries. These are weighted by baryon-violating squark branching fractions and converted into an entropy-normalized yield using 3T/(4m). The numerical treatment includes a 28/79 sphaleron conversion factor above the stated thermal threshold.

sources.title: Electroweak Baryogenesis and the Expansion Rate of the Universe

evidence.text: For homogeneous smooth transitions, use effective CP sources acting as baryon-number or hypercharge chemical potentials to estimate n_B/s at freezeout. Exponential scalar potentials and their attractor solutions motivate possible kination histories.

sources.title: Moduli-induced Baryogenesis

evidence.text: The supersymmetric modulus minimum and its uplift-induced displacement determine FX. Modulus and anomaly contributions to gaugino masses and trilinears are combined to identify the physical CP phase; low-energy soft parameters also depend on renormalization-group evolution.

sources.title: Electroweak Baryogenesis and the Expansion Rate of the Universe

evidence.text: Use the homogeneous scalar conservation equation and Friedmann equation to derive density scaling and expansion histories; include radiation with an instantaneous-decoupling approximation for changes in relativistic degrees of freedom.

sources.title: Electroweak Baryogenesis and the Expansion Rate of the Universe

evidence.text: Compare the post-transition sphaleron rate with H, and integrate the rate to obtain the depletion exponent X in B_f = exp(−X) B(T_o). The sphaleron's exponential temperature dependence localizes washout near the transition.

sources.title: Reconciling Inflation with the Festina Lente Bound through Affleck-Dine Baryogenesis

evidence.text: Can complete gauge symmetry breaking by MSSM flat-direction condensates reconcile inflation with the conditional Festina Lente (FL) argument while enabling Affleck-Dine (AD) baryogenesis consistent with reheating and isocurvature constraints?

sources.title: String loop origin for dark radiation and superheavy dark matter in type IIB compactifications

evidence.text: How do logarithmic string-loop corrections affect perturbative Kähler-modulus stabilization, canonical mixing and axionic dark radiation, and can the resulting modulus reheating support nonthermal dark matter and a baryon–dark matter coincidence?

sources.title: Moduli induced cogenesis of baryon asymmetry and dark matter

evidence.text: Can late modulus decay generate both visible baryon asymmetry and asymmetric dark matter at GeV-scale reheating, while conserving baryon number at the fundamental vertices and explaining ΩDM/ΩB ≈ 5?

sources.title: Leptogenesis in Cosmological Relaxation with Particle Production

evidence.text: Can post-inflationary relaxion particle production explain the weak hierarchy, reheat the visible universe and generate its baryon asymmetry through leptogenesis, without additional particles below the SM EFT cutoff?

sources.title: Higgs, Moduli Problem, Baryogenesis and Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: Can Affleck–Dine baryogenesis survive entropy production from light-modulus decay in high-scale supersymmetry, while LARGE volume stabilization avoids gravitino and LSP overproduction? The paper also examines Q-ball formation and enhanced inflaton–AD couplings.

sources.title: Affleck-Dine Baryogenesis in Type IIB String Models

evidence.text: Can Affleck–Dine baryogenesis be embedded in sequestered type IIB models, with an inflationary tachyonic AD mass, positive late-time scalar masses, and sufficient asymmetry after dilution by the lightest modulus?

sources.title: The Baryon-Dark Matter Ratio Via Moduli Decay After Affleck-Dine Baryogenesis

evidence.text: Can late moduli decay simultaneously dilute excessive MSSM Affleck–Dine baryogenesis, produce the nonthermal LSP abundance, and explain the historical abundance ratio Ωdm/ΩB ≈ 5?

sources.title: Cosmological moduli problem in large volume scenario and thermal inflation

evidence.text: When can single or double thermal inflation dilute the light LVS volume modulus sufficiently despite thermally induced modulus reproduction, and can a concrete model also retain successful baryogenesis and dark matter production?
